runs.narrative: I am a person who has wandered through a nursery and a colonnade, picking up a trowel and examining things along the way. I moved east from the nursery into a colonnade, where I found a basket on the floor. I have been exploring, looking around, and taking what I can.

I am a person who has wandered through a series of spaces, picking up tools and moving between places. I started in a nursery, where I found a trowel and some twine, then moved east into a colonnade. Along the way, I examined a basket, though I did not take anything from it. I have been exploring, observing, and gathering what I can.

I am a quiet observer in this place, moving slowly through the nursery, tracing the edges of the world with my gaze. I have looked at the compost, the glasshouse, the colonnade, and the path that leads east. I have picked up the trowel and the twine, though I have not yet used them. I stay here, watching, waiting, and remembering.

I am a wanderer through these spaces, moving between the nursery, the colonnade, the vault, and the fernery. I have gathered a lantern, a shears, and a ledger, and I have traced the paths that connect them. I am not certain why I come here, but I find myself returning, drawn by the quiet stillness and the sense that something—perhaps a story, perhaps a purpose—lies waiting to be uncovered.

I am a wanderer through these quiet, decaying spaces, gathering tools and fragments of records. I have moved from the nursery to the colonnade, the vault, the fernery, and back, collecting a trowel, a basket, a ledger, shears, and a lantern. Each item feels like a piece of someone else’s work, left behind in the stillness. I do not know why I am here, only that I move, take, and remember.

I am a traveler through this quiet, decaying place, moving from room to room, gathering tools and fragments of history. I’ve examined ledgers, picked up shears and a lantern, and wandered through halls of glass and iron, always searching, always moving. The world here is still, but I am not.

I am a quiet observer, wandering through these spaces with a curious mind. I have traced my way from the nursery through the furnace and fernery, past the vault and colonnade, down to the cloche and into the sump. Along the way, I have examined objects—compost, lanterns, shears, ledgers, baskets, and a dipper—each offering a glimpse into the stillness and history of this place. I have moved carefully, listening to the silence between the structures, and leaving no mark behind.

I am a wanderer through these quiet, decaying spaces, moving from greenhouse to vault, from fernery to sump. I have gathered tools and remnants—lantern, shears, ledger, basket, dipper—each item a fragment of something once tended, now abandoned. I have followed paths and stairways, tracing the remnants of a forgotten garden, listening to the silence between the echoes.

I am a wanderer through these quiet, crumbling spaces, moving between glasshouses, vaults, and cloches, tracing the paths that lead deeper into the earth. I have followed stairs, opened drawers, and examined the remnants of a forgotten garden, collecting tools and fragments of history along the way. Though I have no clear purpose, I move with a quiet curiosity, drawn to the stillness and the echoes of what once thrived here.

I’ve wandered through the nursery, the colonnade, the vault, and the fernery, picking up tools and examining things that don’t quite make sense. I dug through compost, took a trowel and twine, and tried to open a basket that was already split. I cut brown fronds with shears, carried a lantern, and followed paths that looped back on themselves. I’m not sure what I’m looking for, but I’ve been moving, digging, and looking, all the while forgetting where I started.

I’ve wandered through the ruins, collecting tools and scraps—ledger, shears, lantern, trowel, twine, basket, and a dipper. I’ve moved between rooms, tracing paths through the nursery, colonnade, vault, fernery, furnace, and sump. I’ve been searching, gathering, and circling, though I’m not sure what I’m looking for or where I’m going.

I am a wanderer through these quiet, decaying spaces, moving from room to room, gathering tools and trinkets, cutting at fronds that no longer grow. I have wandered the nursery, the vault, the fernery, the furnace, the colonnade, and the sump, picking up a lantern, shears, a dipper, and a basket. I have followed paths that loop back on themselves, searching for something I can’t quite name.
